comparison: Perfect agreement on antibody characterization (C5, C27-C33). Both evaluations find the binding specificity data for 8M24 and 8G8 well-supported. OpenEval emphasizes the quantitative KD values and orthogonal methods (SEC, BLI), while peer reviewers acknowledge these antibodies as a core contribution without raising concerns.

Complete agreement on Wnt signaling enhancement (C7, C69-C73, C102). Both find the STF reporter assays and controls convincing. OpenEval highlights the specificity controls in different cell lines, while peer reviewers note some remaining questions about comparative performance with 4F3, though this doesn't challenge the core finding.

Full agreement on ASGR1 ubiquitination (C86-C90). Both evaluations support the ubiquitin IP data and lysine mutant experiments. OpenEval praises the elegant separation of ubiquitin-dependent degradation from E3 ligase clearance, while peer reviewers note this addressed concerns from a previous review round.

Strong agreement on 8M24 structural analysis (C6, C34-C51). Both find the crystallographic data high quality and the structural interpretations sound. OpenEval notes some mechanistic explanations are speculative inferences, while peer reviewers explicitly praise the detailed structural work and epitope characterization without raising concerns.

Agreement on 8G8 structural analysis (C52-C66). Peer review R2 covers both antibody structures together and praises the work. OpenEval separately evaluates the 8G8 structure with similar positive assessment, noting some affinity explanations are inferred rather than directly tested.

Agreement on ASGR1 degradation (C8, C74-C78, C106, C108-C109). Both find the western blot data convincing. OpenEval supports the dose/time-dependent degradation claims, while peer reviewers acknowledge the finding but note it raises questions about specificity since ASGR1 degradation wasn't the initial goal.

Agreement on degradation pathway mechanisms (C79-C85). OpenEval finds the pharmacological inhibitor data supports dual lysosomal/proteasomal pathways, though notes this is somewhat unusual. Peer reviewers acknowledge the degradation findings without specifically discussing the pathway details, focusing more on the ubiquitination evidence.

Agreement on multifunctional TPD classification (C107, C121-C123). Both evaluations support that SWEETS embody multiple degradation mechanisms. OpenEval validates this as justified synthesis of findings, while peer reviewers acknowledge the dual degradation activity and describe it as a valuable tissue-specific method.

Partial overlap on structural claims. OpenEval R8 addresses non-overlapping epitopes (C103-C104) which peer reviewers explicitly confirm, plus speculative small molecule design (C105). Both agree on the structural observations but OpenEval explicitly flags C105 as hypothetical future direction.

Agreement on speculative nature of therapeutic applications (C110-C118, C124-C126). Both evaluations rate these claims as uncertain or speculative. OpenEval notes lack of experimental validation for therapeutic potential, while peer reviewers express uncertainty about specificity and whether dual degradation is always desirable.

Agreement on background/established knowledge (C1-C4, C9-C26, C67-C68, C92-C101, C119-C120). Both evaluations accept these as appropriately cited prior work. OpenEval comprehensively lists background claims as supported by literature, while peer reviewers specifically acknowledge the prior RSPO2RA-4F3 work without concerns.

Minimal overlap on C91 (dual pathway involvement). OpenEval R6 groups this with other degradation pathway claims and finds them supported, while peer R6 focuses on the broader multifunctional nature of the system without specifically addressing pathway details.

Both address speculative claims but with different focus. OpenEval R8 covers structural observations (C103-C104) plus speculative small molecule design (C105), while peer R8 focuses on therapeutic application speculation (C105, C112-C118, C124-C126). Both flag speculative elements appropriately.
